title: Fictional Vehicle Digital Access Specification — Educational Demo Only
disclaimer: Entirely independently authored hypothetical requirements. NOT CCC Digital Key Specification, NOT actual 3.1.4 or 4.1.0 requirements, and not evidence of compliance. Version labels V1/V2 are fictional.

requirements.heading: Owner Device Provisioning
requirements.text: In this fictional protocol, a vehicle SHALL create an owner-device record only after a local enrollment challenge is completed and approved by the vehicle display.

requirements.heading: Offline Initial Pairing
requirements.text: If the fictional vehicle is offline, initial owner pairing MAY proceed using a local enrollment token; cloud synchronization SHALL be deferred until connectivity returns.

requirements.heading: Friend Key Sharing
requirements.text: A fictional owner device MAY issue a friend-device invitation only when key sharing is enabled and the friend is assigned an explicit entitlement set.

requirements.heading: Delegated Sharing
requirements.text: In this fictional V1 profile, a friend device SHALL NOT create another invitation, even when the original owner permitted vehicle access.

requirements.heading: Key Revocation
requirements.text: After a fictional key is marked revoked, the access controller SHALL reject subsequent operations using that credential; a wireless connection alone SHALL NOT restore authorization.

requirements.heading: Temporary Suspension
requirements.text: The fictional owner MAY suspend a friend credential without deleting it. A suspended credential SHALL NOT authorize access until an owner-approved resume event is recorded.

requirements.heading: BLE Discovery
requirements.text: For this fictional demo, a mobile device SHOULD use BLE discovery to identify a nearby vehicle before initiating an access session; discovery SHALL NOT by itself grant access.

requirements.heading: BLE Connection Failure
requirements.text: If a fictional BLE connection attempt times out, the mobile device MAY retry once after a user-visible delay; it SHALL NOT treat the failed attempt as successful authentication.

requirements.heading: UWB Passive Entry
requirements.text: When passive entry is enabled, the fictional vehicle SHALL require a valid credential, a completed challenge response, and an acceptable UWB distance estimate before unlocking.

requirements.heading: Ranging Unavailable
requirements.text: If fictional UWB ranging cannot be completed, passive entry SHALL stop; the user MAY attempt the separate NFC tap-to-access procedure if enabled.

requirements.heading: NFC Tap-to-Access
requirements.text: For a fictional NFC entry operation, a valid credential and an explicit tap event SHALL be verified. NFC access SHALL NOT require a successful prior UWB ranging session.

requirements.heading: Operation Entitlements
requirements.text: Every fictional access request SHALL be checked against the credential's allowed operations. Entry-only access SHALL NOT imply permission to start the vehicle.

requirements.heading: Time-Limited Access
requirements.text: When a fictional shared credential has an active-time window, access SHALL be rejected outside the configured window regardless of successful BLE discovery.

requirements.heading: Offline Operation
requirements.text: While the fictional vehicle is offline, previously activated local credentials MAY be evaluated, but pending invitation approvals SHALL wait for network access.

requirements.heading: Minimal Event Logging
requirements.text: For fictional audit trails, the system SHALL record a non-identifying event category and outcome, and SHOULD avoid storing raw device identifiers in diagnostic exports.

requirements.heading: User-Facing Error
requirements.text: A fictional client SHALL distinguish 'credential not authorized' from 'radio not available' in its error category without displaying secret key material.

requirements.heading: Purpose and Scope
requirements.text: In this fictional specification, a digital key is a credential stored on a mobile device, such as a smartphone, that lets an authorized user unlock, lock, or start a vehicle without a physical key. This document is an independently authored educational demo, not an official specification.

requirements.heading: Feature Summary
requirements.text: This fictional digital key covers owner device provisioning (2.1), friend key sharing and delegation (2.2), revocation and suspension (2.3), BLE discovery, UWB passive entry and NFC tap-to-access (3.x), operation entitlements and time limits (4.1), offline operation (4.2), and privacy-preserving logging and error reporting (5.x).

requirements.heading: Terms
requirements.text: In this fictional document, an owner device is the first device provisioned for a vehicle; a friend device receives a shared key from the owner; a credential is the key data a device presents; an entitlement is an allowed operation such as entry or start; passive entry unlocks the vehicle when an authorized device is verified nearby without a user action.
